2 تمّر , inf. n. تَتْمِيرٌ, He dried (S, M, K) dates. (S.) ―
-b2- (tropical:) He dried flesh-meat: (T, S:) or he cut flesh-meat into small pieces, (M, A, * IAth, K,) like dates, (IAth,) and dried it. (M, A, IAth, K.) It is said in a trad., كَانَ لَا يَرَى بِالتَّتْمِيرِ بَأْسًا (tropical:) He used not to see any harm in cutting flesh-meat into small pieces, like dates, and drying it: meaning, in a Mohrim's thus preparing flesh-meat for travelling-provision; or in one's drying the flesh of wild animals before the state of ihrám. (IAth.) ―
-b3- See also 1: ―
-b4- and 4, in two places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
